newsitem.title: USA: Conseco to buy Transport Holdings.
newsitem.headline: Conseco to buy Transport Holdings.

text.p: Conseco Inc. will acquire Transport Holdings Inc., a provider of cancer and supplemental health insurance, for $311 million in stock, the companies said Thursday.

The deal is the sixth announced or completed by Conseco so far in 1996, boosting the Carmel, Ind.-based insurance holding company's investments under management to $31 billion and assets on its own balance sheet to $27 billion.
News of the deal sent Transport's stock surging $16.25, more than 31 percent, to $68 on Nasdaq, where it was the top gainer. Conseco rose 62.5 cents to $47.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The purchase price, equal to $70 a share, includes $228 million for Transport's 3.2 million common shares and equivalents and $83 million to retire bank debt and preferred stock, the companies said.
Transport will be merged into Conseco, which owns and operates life insurance companies and provides investment management, administrative and other fee-based services.
Fort Worth, Texas-based Transport's principal subsidiary, Transport Life Insurance Co., specialises in supplemental life and health insurance.
Transport's board may evaluate other offers to the extent required by its fiduciary duties, but it is required to pay a break-up fee if it calls off the merger with Conseco.

Conseco Chairman Stephen Hilbert said his company aims to be a leader in each of its major product lines, including supplemental health insurance, retirement savings annuities and universal life insurance.

He said Conseco is focusing exclusively on acquisitions that complement its long-term business strategy, maintain earnings momentum and maintain a conservative capital structure, with debt no more than 35 percent of total capital.

Upon completion of Conseco's six acquisitions this year, it will have $7.0 billion in annual premiums and revenues, $4.8 billion of equity market capitalisation and more than $690 million of projected annual earnings before interest and taxes. Total capital will approach $5.6 billion.
Conseco said Transport, with about $110 million in annual premiums and $600 million of assets, is expected to add about 7 cents per fully diluted share to its 1997 earnings.
Conseco's other acquisitions this year are Life Partners Group, American Travellers Corp., American Financial Corp., Bankers Life Holding Corp. and American Life Holdings, Inc.

Under the agreement announced Thursday, each Transport class A common stock would be converted into the right to receive Conseco common stock. The number of shares would not be more than 1.8301, nor less than 1.40, they said.
Transport's outstanding convertible debt, stock options and warrants, when converted or exercised, would receive the same ratio of Carmel, Ind.-based Conseco shares.
The deal is expected to close by the end of 1996, subject to approval by Transport stockholders and regulators.
